title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 15. The Joyous Meeting with Sri Paramananda Puri
html:
The Lord reveals to Ramananda Raya the secret of the pastimes of Vrindavana, passes through Panchavati and Shrirangam, spends the rainy season with the brahmana Trimalla and blesses his son Gopala, and on the way back meets Paramananda Puri

Verse 1

ततः प्रभाते विमले शुभे प्रभु-
र्गायन्हरिं प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्यः।
ययौ स काञ्चीनगरं जगद्गुरु-
र्द्रष्टुं श्रीरामानन्दाख्यरायम्॥१॥

tataḥ prabhāte vimale śubhe prabhu-
rgāyanhariṁ premavibhinnadhairyaḥ|
yayau sa kāñcīnagaraṁ jagadguru-
rdraṣṭuṁ śrīrāmānandākhyarāyam||1||

tatah — then; prabhate — in the morning; vimale — clear; shubhe — auspicious; prabhuh — the Lord; gayan — singing; harim — Hari; prema-vibhinna-dhairyah — His composure broken by love; yayau — went; sah — He; kanchi-nagaram — to the city of Kanchi; jagat-guruh — the Teacher of the world; drashtum — to see; shri-ramananda-akhya-rayam — the Raya named Sri Ramananda.

1Then, on a clear and auspicious morning, the Lord, the Teacher of the world, singing of Hari, His composure quite broken by love, set out for the city of Kanchi to see Sri Ramananda Raya1.

Verse 2

स स्वगृहे कृष्णपूजावसाने
ध्यायन्परं ब्रह्म व्रजेन्द्रनन्दनम्।
ददर्श वारत्रयमद्भुतं मह-
द्गौराङ्गमाधुर्यमतीव विस्मितः॥२॥

sa svagṛhe kṛṣṇapūjāvasāne
dhyāyanparaṁ brahma vrajendranandanam|
dadarśa vāratrayamadbhutaṁ maha-
dgaurāṅgamādhuryamatīva vismitaḥ||2||

sah — he; sva-grihe — in his own house; krishna-puja-avasane — at the end of his worship of Krishna; dhyayan — meditating on; param brahma — the Supreme Brahman; vraja-indra-nandanam — the son of the king of Vraja; dadarsha — beheld; vara-trayam — three times; adbhutam — wondrous; mahat — great; gauranga-madhuryam — the sweetness of Gauranga; ativa — exceedingly; vismitah — astonished.

2Ramananda, in his own house, having finished his worship of Krishna, was meditating on the Supreme Brahman, the son of the king of Vraja — and three times he beheld the great and wondrous sweetness of Gauranga, and was utterly astonished.

Verse 3

उन्मील्य नेत्रे च तदेव रूपं
दृष्ट्वा परं ब्रह्म सन्न्यासवेशम्।
प्रणम्य मूर्ध्ना विहितः कृताञ्जलिः
पप्रच्छ कुत्रत्यो भवानिति प्रभो॥३॥

unmīlya netre ca tadeva rūpaṁ
dṛṣṭvā paraṁ brahma sannyāsaveśam|
praṇamya mūrdhnā vihitaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
papraccha kutratyo bhavāniti prabho||3||

unmilya — opening; netre — his eyes; cha — and; tat eva — that very; rupam — form; drishtva — seeing; param brahma — the Supreme Brahman; sannyasa-vesham — in the dress of a sannyasi; pranamya — bowing; murdhna — with his head; vihitah — having done (the obeisance); krita-anjalih — with joined palms; papraccha — asked; kutratyah — from where; bhavan — Your Honour; iti — thus; prabho — O Lord.

3Opening his eyes, he saw that very form — the Supreme Brahman in the dress of a sannyasi. Bowing his head to the ground and joining his palms, he asked, "Where have You come from, my Lord?"

Verse 4

हसन्प्रभुः प्राह कथं न स्मर्यते
श्रीराधिकापादसरोजषट्पद।
स्वात्मानमेवं कथयन्स्वयं हरिः
स्वबाहुयुग्मेन तमालिलिङ्ग॥४॥

hasanprabhuḥ prāha kathaṁ na smaryate
śrīrādhikāpādasarojaṣaṭpada|
svātmānamevaṁ kathayansvayaṁ hariḥ
svabāhuyugmena tamāliliṅga||4||

hasan — laughing; prabhuh — the Lord; praha — said; katham — how; na — not; smaryate — is it remembered; shri-radhika-pada-saroja-shatpada — O bee at the lotus feet of Sri Radhika; sva-atmanam — Himself; evam — thus; kathayan — making known; svayam — Himself; harih — Hari; sva-bahu-yugmena — with both His arms; tam — him; alilinga — embraced.

4The Lord laughed and said, "How can you not remember, O bee at the lotus feet of Sri Radhika?" And having thus made Himself known, Hari Himself embraced him with both arms.

Verse 5

वृन्दाटवीकेलिरहस्यमद्भुतं
प्रकाश्य तस्मिन्रसिकेन्द्रमौलिः।
आज्ञाप्य क्षेत्रगमनाय सत्वरं
तं सान्त्वयित्वा स ययौ जनार्दनः॥५॥

vṛndāṭavīkelirahasyamadbhutaṁ
prakāśya tasminrasikendramauliḥ|
ājñāpya kṣetragamanāya satvaraṁ
taṁ sāntvayitvā sa yayau janārdanaḥ||5||

vrindatavi-keli-rahasyam — the secret of the pastimes in the forest of Vrinda; adbhutam — wondrous; prakashya — revealing; tasmin — to him; rasika-indra-maulih — the crown of the kings of rasikas; ajnapya — commanding; kshetra-gamanaya — to go to Kshetra; satvaram — quickly; tam — him; santvayitva — comforting; sah — He; yayau — departed; janardanah — Janardana.

5The crown of the kings of rasikas revealed to him the wondrous secret of the pastimes in the forest of Vrinda, bade him go quickly to Kshetra2, and, having comforted him, Janardana went His way.

Verse 6

श्रीराम गोविन्द कृष्णेति गाय-
न्नुत्तीर्य गोदावरीमेव कृष्णः।
विवेश श्रीपञ्चवटीवनं मह-
च्छ्रीरामसीतास्मरणातिविह्वलः॥६॥

śrīrāma govinda kṛṣṇeti gāya-
nnuttīrya godāvarīmeva kṛṣṇaḥ|
viveśa śrīpañcavaṭīvanaṁ maha-
cchrīrāmasītāsmaraṇātivihvalaḥ||6||

shri-rama — "Sri Rama!"; govinda — "Govinda!"; krishna-iti — "Krishna!" — thus; gayan — singing; uttirya — crossing; godavarim — the Godavari; eva — indeed; krishnah — Krishna; vivesha — entered; shri-panchavati-vanam — the forest of Sri Panchavati; mahat — great; shri-rama-sita-smarana-ati-vihvalah — overwhelmed by the remembrance of Sri Rama and Sita.

6Singing "Sri Rama! Govinda! Krishna!", Krishna crossed the Godavari and entered the great forest of Sri Panchavati3, overwhelmed by the remembrance of Sri Rama and Sita.

Verse 7

ततः परं श्रीजगदीश्वरः प्रभु-
श्चलन्पृथिव्यां ककुभः प्रकाशयन्।
कावेरीमुत्तीर्य श्रीरङ्गनाथं
दृष्ट्वातिहृष्टो हि ननर्त सादरम्॥७॥

tataḥ paraṁ śrījagadīśvaraḥ prabhu-
ścalanpṛthivyāṁ kakubhaḥ prakāśayan|
kāverīmuttīrya śrīraṅganāthaṁ
dṛṣṭvātihṛṣṭo hi nanarta sādaram||7||

tatah param — after that; shri-jagat-ishvarah — Sri Lord of the world; prabhuh — the Lord; chalan — walking; prithivyam — over the earth; kakubhah — the quarters; prakashayan — illuminating; kaverim — the Kaveri; uttirya — crossing; shri-ranganatham — Sri Ranganatha; drishtva — seeing; ati-hrishtah — overjoyed; hi — indeed; nanarta — danced; sa-adaram — reverently.

7Then Sri Jagadishvara, the Lord, walked on over the earth, lighting up every quarter of the sky; crossing the Kaveri, He beheld Sri Ranganatha4 and, in great joy, reverently danced.

Verse 8

श्रीरङ्गनाथस्य समीपं विप्रो
गीतां पठन्शुद्धविचारशून्यम्।
प्रेमाश्रुपूर्णं स निरीक्ष्य कृष्ण
आलिङ्ग्य प्राह श्रुतमेव योग्यम्॥८॥

śrīraṅganāthasya samīpaṁ vipro
gītāṁ paṭhanśuddhavicāraśūnyam|
premāśrupūrṇaṁ sa nirīkṣya kṛṣṇa
āliṅgya prāha śrutameva yogyam||8||

shri-ranganathasya — of Sri Ranganatha; samipam — near; viprah — a brahmana; gitam — the Gita; pathan — reciting; shuddha-vichara-shunyam — without correct understanding; prema-ashru-purnam — full of tears of love; sah — He; nirikshya — seeing; krishnah — Krishna; alingya — embracing; praha — said; shrutam — learning of scripture; eva — indeed; yogyam — fitting.

8Near Sri Ranganatha a brahmana was reciting the Gita without properly understanding it; but seeing him filled with tears of love, Krishna embraced him and said, "This indeed is true learning in scripture!"5

Verse 9

तत्रैव कश्चिद्द्विजवर्यसत्तमो
दृष्ट्वा प्रभुं गौरसुदीर्घविग्रहम्।
प्रेमाश्रुपूर्णं स जगाद बन्धुं
श्रीकृष्णवर्णं मनसा विचारयन्॥९॥

tatraiva kaściddvijavaryasattamo
dṛṣṭvā prabhuṁ gaurasudīrghavigraham|
premāśrupūrṇaṁ sa jagāda bandhuṁ
śrīkṛṣṇavarṇaṁ manasā vicārayan||9||

tatra eva — right there; kashchit — a certain; dvija-varya-sattamah — best of excellent brahmanas; drishtva — seeing; prabhum — the Lord; gaura-sudirgha-vigraham — of golden and tall form; prema-ashru-purnam — full of tears of love; sah — he; jagada — spoke; bandhum — to his kinsman; shri-krishna-varnam — (that He is) "Krishna-varna"; manasa — in his mind; vicharayan — considering.

9There, too, a certain excellent brahmana, foremost among the worthy, seeing the Lord — tall, golden, and filled with tears of love — concluded in his mind that this was the One called "Krishna-varna"6, and said so to his kinsman.

Verse 10

अहो स्वभाग्यं मनसा विमृश्य
त्रिमल्लनामा किल भट्टराजः।
तस्य प्रभोः श्रीचरणं कराभ्यां
धृत्वा प्रहृष्टः करुणां न्यवेदयत्॥१०॥

aho svabhāgyaṁ manasā vimṛśya
trimallanāmā kila bhaṭṭarājaḥ|
tasya prabhoḥ śrīcaraṇaṁ karābhyāṁ
dhṛtvā prahṛṣṭaḥ karuṇāṁ nyavedayat||10||

aho — oh!; sva-bhagyam — his good fortune; manasa — in his mind; vimrishya — reflecting on; trimalla-nama — named Trimalla; kila — indeed; bhatta-rajah — the king of Bhattas (a learned brahmana); tasya — of that; prabhoh — Lord; shri-charanam — the holy feet; karabhyam — with both hands; dhritva — clasping; prahrishtah — overjoyed; karunam — a plaintive plea; nyavedayat — made known.

10Thinking, "Oh, what good fortune is mine!", the Bhatta-raja named Trimalla7 clasped the Lord's holy feet in both hands and, overjoyed, made his heartfelt plea:

Verse 11

अहो महात्मन्करुणेन नः प्रभो
कृपां विधातुं सततं त्वमर्हसि।
तत्रैव मायाधमनावतारे
कृपामृतेनापि जगत्सिषेच॥११॥

aho mahātmankaruṇena naḥ prabho
kṛpāṁ vidhātuṁ satataṁ tvamarhasi|
tatraiva māyādhamanāvatāre
kṛpāmṛtenāpi jagatsiṣeca||11||

aho — oh!; maha-atman — great soul; karunena — out of compassion; nah — to us; prabho — O Lord; kripam — mercy; vidhatum — to show; satatam — always; tvam — You; arhasi — ought; tatra eva — in this very; maya-dhamana-avatare — descent that blows away maya; kripa-amritena — with the nectar of mercy; api — and; jagat — the world; sisheca — has sprinkled.

11"O great soul, O Lord! Out of compassion You must ever show us mercy — for in this very descent, which blows away maya, You have drenched the world with the nectar of mercy.

Verse 12

सर्वं जनं स्थावरजङ्गमादी-
नुद्धर्तुमन्यो न विनापि कृष्णम्।
प्रावृडृतुरागत एव नाथ
भृत्यस्य मे त्वं हितशोभनं कुरु॥१२॥

sarvaṁ janaṁ sthāvarajaṅgamādī-
nuddhartumanyo na vināpi kṛṣṇam|
prāvṛḍṛturāgata eva nātha
bhṛtyasya me tvaṁ hitaśobhanaṁ kuru||12||

sarvam — all; janam — people; sthavara-jangama-adin — the unmoving, the moving and the rest; uddhartum — to deliver; anyah — another; na — not (can); vina — without; api — even; krishnam — Krishna; pravrit-rituh — the rainy season; agatah — has come; eva — already; natha — O Master; bhrityasya — for the servant; me — me; tvam — You; hita-shobhanam — what is good and fair; kuru — do.

12None but Krishna can deliver all people — the unmoving creatures and the moving and all the rest. And now the rainy season has come, O Master: do what is good and fair for me, Your servant."8

Verse 13

एवं स भक्तस्य मधुरां सुवाणीं
श्रुत्वा तमालिङ्ग्य विवेश तद्गृहम्।
द्विजोऽपि तत्पादसरोरुहं सुधीः
प्रक्षाल्य प्रेम्णा सगणो दधार॥१३॥

evaṁ sa bhaktasya madhurāṁ suvāṇīṁ
śrutvā tamāliṅgya viveśa tadgṛham|
dvijo'pi tatpādasaroruhaṁ sudhīḥ
prakṣālya premṇā sagaṇo dadhāra||13||

evam — such; sah — He; bhaktasya — of His devotee; madhuram — sweet; suvanim — fair words; shrutva — hearing; tam — him; alingya — embracing; vivesha — entered; tat-griham — his house; dvijah — the brahmana; api — too; tat-pada-saroruham — His lotus feet; sudhih — wise; prakshalya — washing; premna — with love; sa-ganah — with his people; dadhara — took (that water).

13Hearing these sweet and lovely words of His devotee, the Lord embraced him and entered his house. And the wise brahmana washed His lotus feet and, together with all his household, lovingly received that water.

Verse 14

सुखासीनं जगन्नाथं त्रिमल्लाख्यो द्विजोत्तमः।
स्त्रीपुत्रस्वजनैः सार्धं सिषेवे प्रेमनिर्भरः॥१४॥

sukhāsīnaṁ jagannāthaṁ trimallākhyo dvijottamaḥ|
strīputrasvajanaiḥ sārdhaṁ siṣeve premanirbharaḥ||14||

sukha-asinam — comfortably seated; jagannatham — the Lord of the world; trimalla-akhyah — named Trimalla; dvija-uttamah — the best of brahmanas; stri-putra-sva-janaih — with wife, sons and kinsfolk; sardham — together; sisheve — served; prema-nirbharah — full of love.

14When the Lord of the world was seated at His ease, the best of brahmanas named Trimalla, overflowing with love, served Him together with his wife, his sons and all his kinsfolk.

Verse 15

गोपालनामा बालोऽस्य प्रभोः पार्श्वे स्थितस्तदा।
तं दृष्ट्वा तस्य शिरसि पादपद्मं दयार्द्रधीः॥१५॥

gopālanāmā bālo'sya prabhoḥ pārśve sthitastadā|
taṁ dṛṣṭvā tasya śirasi pādapadmaṁ dayārdradhīḥ||15||

gopala-nama — named Gopala; balah — boy; asya — his (Trimalla's); prabhoh — of the Lord; parshve — at the side; sthitah — stood; tada — then; tam — him; drishtva — seeing; tasya — his; shirasi — on the head; pada-padmam — lotus foot; daya-ardra-dhih — His heart melting with compassion.

15His little boy named Gopala9 was then standing at the Lord's side. Seeing him, the Lord, His heart melting with compassion,

Verse 16

दत्त्वा वद हरिं चेति सोऽपि हर्षसमन्वितः।
बाल्यक्रीडां परित्यज्य कृष्णं गायन्ननर्त च॥१६॥

dattvā vada hariṁ ceti so'pi harṣasamanvitaḥ|
bālyakrīḍāṁ parityajya kṛṣṇaṁ gāyannanarta ca||16||

dattva — placing; vada — say; harim — "Hari"; cha — and; iti — thus (saying); sah — he; api — for his part; harsha-samanvitah — filled with joy; balya-kridam — childish play; parityajya — giving up; krishnam — Krishna; gayan — singing; nanarta — danced; cha — and.

16placed His lotus foot on the boy's head and said, "Say 'Hari'!" And the boy, filled with joy, gave up his childish games and began to sing of Krishna and to dance.

Verse 17

एवं हि प्रावृट्समयं स्थितो हरिः
श्रीकृष्णसङ्कीर्तनभावभावुकः।
श्रीरङ्गक्षेत्रस्थद्विजैः सुपूजितो
भिक्षान्नपानादिभिरच्युतः सुखम्॥१७॥

evaṁ hi prāvṛṭsamayaṁ sthito hariḥ
śrīkṛṣṇasaṅkīrtanabhāvabhāvukaḥ|
śrīraṅgakṣetrasthadvijaiḥ supūjito
bhikṣānnapānādibhiracyutaḥ sukham||17||

evam — thus; hi — indeed; pravrit-samayam — through the rainy season; sthitah — stayed; harih — Hari; shri-krishna-sankirtana-bhava-bhavukah — absorbed in the mood of the sankirtana of Sri Krishna; shri-ranga-kshetra-stha-dvijaih — by the brahmanas of Sri Ranga-kshetra; su-pujitah — well honoured; bhiksha-anna-pana-adibhih — with alms of food, drink and so on; achyutah — the Infallible; sukham — happily.

17Thus Hari, the Infallible, absorbed in the mood of the sankirtana of Sri Krishna, happily spent the rainy season there, honoured by the brahmanas of Sri Ranga-kshetra with alms of food and drink and the like.

Verse 18

मेरुसुन्दरतनू रसिकेशः
कृष्णनामगुणकीर्तनमत्तः।
राधिकारसविनोदगद्गद-
प्रेमवारिपरिपूरितदेहः॥१८॥

merusundaratanū rasikeśaḥ
kṛṣṇanāmaguṇakīrtanamattaḥ|
rādhikārasavinodagadgada-
premavāriparipūritadehaḥ||18||

meru-sundara-tanuh — whose body is beautiful as Mount Meru; rasika-ishah — the Lord of rasikas; krishna-nama-guna-kirtana-mattah — intoxicated with chanting the names and qualities of Krishna; radhika-rasa-vinoda-gadgada — His voice faltering with the delight of Radhika's rasa; prema-vari-paripurita-dehah — His body flooded with the waters of love.

18The Lord of rasikas, whose body was beautiful as Mount Meru10, was intoxicated with chanting the names and qualities of Krishna; His voice faltered with the delight of Radhika's rasa, and His body was flooded with the waters of love.

Verse 19

उषित्वैवं रङ्गक्षेत्राद्गच्छन्पथि ददर्श सः।
श्रीमाधवपुरीशिष्यं परमानन्दनामकम्॥१९॥

uṣitvaivaṁ raṅgakṣetrādgacchanpathi dadarśa saḥ|
śrīmādhavapurīśiṣyaṁ paramānandanāmakam||19||

ushitva — having stayed; evam — thus; ranga-kshetrat — from Ranga-kshetra; gacchan — going; pathi — on the road; dadarsha — saw; sah — He; shri-madhava-puri-shishyam — the disciple of Sri Madhava Puri; paramananda-namakam — named Paramananda.

19Having stayed thus at Ranga-kshetra, He went on, and on the road He met a disciple of Sri Madhava Puri11 named Paramananda.

Verse 20

पश्यञ्छ्रीपरमानन्दपुरी गौराङ्गविग्रहम्।
गुरुवाक्यमनुस्मृत्य प्रेमाश्रुपुलकाञ्चितः॥२०॥

paśyañchrīparamānandapurī gaurāṅgavigraham|
guruvākyamanusmṛtya premāśrupulakāñcitaḥ||20||

pashyan — seeing; shri-paramananda-puri — Sri Paramananda Puri; gauranga-vigraham — the form of Gauranga; guru-vakyam — his guru's words; anusmritya — remembering; prema-ashru-pulaka-anchitah — adorned with tears of love and thrilling hair.

20Seeing the form of Gauranga, Sri Paramananda Puri remembered his guru's words, and was adorned with tears of love and thrilling hair.

Verse 21

ईश्वरोऽपि पुरीपादं सभृत्यं धर्मपालकः।
ननाम परमप्रीतो दण्डवच्छिरसा भुवि॥२१॥

īśvaro'pi purīpādaṁ sabhṛtyaṁ dharmapālakaḥ|
nanāma paramaprīto daṇḍavacchirasā bhuvi||21||

ishvarah — the Lord; api — too; puri-padam — to Puripada; sa-bhrityam — with his servant; dharma-palakah — the guardian of dharma; nanama — bowed; parama-pritah — in supreme delight; danda-vat — like a stick; shirasa — with His head; bhuvi — on the ground.

21And the Lord too, the guardian of dharma, in supreme delight fell down like a stick, His head to the ground, before Puripada and his servant.

Verse 22

ससाध्वसं पुरी प्राह मैवं कर्तुमिहार्हसि।
त्वमेव जगतां नाथो जगच्चैतन्यकारकः॥२२॥

sasādhvasaṁ purī prāha maivaṁ kartumihārhasi|
tvameva jagatāṁ nātho jagaccaitanyakārakaḥ||22||

sa-sadhvasam — in alarm; puri — Puri; praha — said; ma — not; evam — so; kartum — to act; iha — here; arhasi — You should; tvam — You; eva — alone; jagatam — of the worlds; nathah — the Lord; jagat-chaitanya-karakah — the One who awakens consciousness in the world.

22In alarm Puri said, "You should not do so! You alone are the Lord of the worlds, the One who awakens consciousness in the world.12

Verse 23

ज्ञातोऽसि भगवान्साक्षाच्छ्रीकृष्णभक्तरूपधृक्।
श्रीराधाभावमापन्नो माधुर्यरसलम्पटः॥२३॥

jñāto'si bhagavānsākṣācchrīkṛṣṇabhaktarūpadhṛk|
śrīrādhābhāvamāpanno mādhuryarasalampaṭaḥ||23||

jnatah — known; asi — You are; bhagavan — Bhagavan; sakshat — Himself; shri-krishna-bhakta-rupa-dhrik — bearing the form of a devotee of Sri Krishna; shri-radha-bhavam — the mood of Sri Radha; apannah — having assumed; madhurya-rasa-lampatah — greedy for the rasa of sweetness.

23I know who You are: You are Bhagavan Himself, who has taken the form of a devotee of Sri Krishna; You have assumed the mood of Sri Radha and thirst for the rasa of sweetness."

Verse 24

श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं कृष्णः प्रहसन्प्राह सादरम्।
प्रेम्णा ते बद्धहृदयं मां जानीहि न संशयः॥२४॥

śrutvā tadvacanaṁ kṛṣṇaḥ prahasanprāha sādaram|
premṇā te baddhahṛdayaṁ māṁ jānīhi na saṁśayaḥ||24||

shrutva — hearing; tat-vachanam — his words; krishnah — Krishna; prahasan — laughing; praha — said; sa-adaram — respectfully; premna — by love; te — your; baddha-hridayam — whose heart is bound; mam — Me; janihi — know; na — no; samshayah — doubt.

24Hearing his words, Krishna laughed and replied respectfully, "Know that My heart is bound by your love — of this there is no doubt.

Verse 25

गच्छ क्षेत्रं महारम्यं यावच्चाहं समाव्रजे।
तावदेव भवांस्तिष्ठत्वेवमुक्त्वा ययौ हरिः॥२५॥

gaccha kṣetraṁ mahāramyaṁ yāvaccāhaṁ samāvraje|
tāvadeva bhavāṁstiṣṭhatvevamuktvā yayau hariḥ||25||

gaccha — go; kshetram — to Kshetra; maha-ramyam — most delightful; yavat — until; cha — and; aham — I; samavraje — return; tavat — till then; eva — indeed; bhavan — Your Honour; tishthatu — should stay; evam — thus; uktva — saying; yayau — went; harih — Hari.

25Go to the most delightful Kshetra and stay there until I return." So saying, Hari went on His way.

Thus ends the fifteenth sarga, "The Joyous Meeting with Sri Paramananda Puri" (Shri-paramananda-puri-sanga-utsava), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Ramananda Raya: a great devotee who governed a southern province under King Prataparudra. Murari Gupta places the meeting in Kanchi; in Krishnadasa Kaviraja's "Chaitanya Charitamrita" it takes place on the bank of the Godavari.
  2. Kshetra (Shri-kshetra): Puri, the abode of Jagannatha.
  3. Panchavati: the forest on the Godavari where Rama and Sita lived in exile.
  4. Ranganatha: Vishnu reclining on the serpent Shesha, at Shrirangam, on an island in the Kaveri.
  5. The same story is told in the "Chaitanya Charitamrita" (Madhya 9): the brahmana knew little Sanskrit, but as he read the Gita he saw Krishna on Arjuna's chariot and wept.
  6. "Krishna-varna": "He who chants the syllables Krish-na", or "He who is called Krishna"; words of the Bhagavata Purana (11.5.32: krishna-varnam tvishakrishnam) which the Gaudiya Vaishnavas apply to Sri Chaitanya.
  7. Trimalla Bhatta: a brahmana of Shrirangam. In the "Chaitanya Charitamrita" the Lord's host is Venkata Bhatta, and Trimalla is his brother.
  8. That is, to stay with him for the four months of the rains (chaturmasya), when sannyasis do not travel.
  9. Gopala: later Gopala Bhatta Gosvami, one of the six Gosvamis of Vrindavana; in later biographies he is the son of Venkata Bhatta.
  10. Meru: the golden mountain at the centre of the world; the comparison speaks of the Lord's golden colour and tall stature.
  11. Madhava Puri: Madhavendra Puri, the guru of Ishvara Puri and of Paramananda Puri.
  12. A play on words in the original: jagac-chaitanya-karaka, "the One who awakens consciousness (chaitanya) in the world", that is, "who gives the world Chaitanya."
